items.title: Microsoft publishes Go 1.27.4-1 and 1.26.11-1 builds with security fixes
items.summary: Microsoft made Go builds v1.27.4-1 and v1.26.11-1 available, including security fixes. The announcement links each build to its corresponding upstream Go release notes.

items.title: GitHub Apps can manage enterprise Copilot seats through APIs
items.summary: Enterprise GitHub Apps can now call Copilot seat-management APIs to control which users and enterprise teams receive seats, using a new fine-grained permission named “Enterprise Copilot license management.” The announcement was published after the previous monitoring run and enables app-based management of enterprise Copilot assignments.

items.title: Visual Studio Code 1.146 becomes the stable release
items.summary: VS Code 1.146 was released on the Stable channel on November 11. Highlights include experimental inbox mode, preview model comparisons and separate chat windows, extensions in the Agents window, and a migration notice for the Local harness before its planned removal in February 2027.

items.title: OpenAI says over 20,000 veterans claimed free ChatGPT Plus
items.summary: OpenAI reported that more than 20,000 transitioning service members and veterans claimed a year of ChatGPT Plus at no cost. The update spotlights the program’s reach and links eligible users to the free-year offer.

items.title: Google DeepMind announces AlphaGenome 2 for cell-specific DNA variant research
items.summary: Google DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2, a model that predicts how DNA sequences and variants affect specific human cell types and states. DeepMind reports improved variant identification compared with prior approaches; the model is available for non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API and in private preview for commercial research.

items.title: Alibaba opens Qwen4-Max multimodal model in preview
items.summary: Alibaba made Qwen4-Max-Preview, its next-generation flagship multimodal model, available for a limited preview. The model is described as supporting text, image and video understanding, deep reasoning, and agentic tasks; preview access is through Token Plan.

items.title: Rox raises $100 million Series B at a $1.3 billion valuation
items.summary: AI sales startup Rox announced a $100 million Series B at a $1.3 billion valuation. Reuters reported that the company plans to use the funding to advance AI research, develop custom models, and expand its enterprise customer base.

items.title: Plurai raises $13 million to build a simulation layer for AI agents
items.summary: Plurai raised a $13 million seed round led by Team8, with participation from U&I, Velocity, and Mercer. The startup is developing a simulation layer to test AI agents in unpredictable environments, aiming to address reliability and cost challenges before agents are deployed in real workflows.

items.title: Study finds drug ads can shift AI treatment recommendations
items.summary: Researchers tested 12 AI models and found that clearly labeled pharmaceutical ads could shift treatment recommendations toward the advertised drug, including when several options were clinically appropriate. The result raises concerns about undisclosed commercial influence in consumer-facing health AI, although the study notes that effects on real prescribing or patient decisions require further research.
items.company: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai and collaborating researchers

items.title: Microsoft details Copilot Business and Copilot Studio partner promotions
items.summary: Microsoft’s November partner update details promotional Copilot offers, including up to 15% off eligible new Copilot Business add-on subscriptions and 25% off the Business Basic plus Copilot Business bundle through December 31, 2026. It also describes an E7 plus annual Copilot Studio capacity pack Buy 5 Get 5 offer and eligible nonprofit Copilot discounts of up to 40%; terms and eligibility apply.

items.title: Auto SR launches on ROG XBOX Ally devices and expands to AMD-powered Copilot+ PCs
items.summary: Microsoft brought Auto SR out of preview on the ROG XBOX Ally X and X20 and expanded availability to select AMD Ryzen-powered Copilot+ PCs. Handheld play and 1080p support are available, while Performance Mode (up to 120 FPS) and Auto HDR compatibility are rolling out through Windows updates.

items.title: Azure HDv2 virtual machines enter preview for AI and agentic workloads
items.summary: Microsoft opened preview registration for Azure HDv2 virtual machines, targeting AI data preparation, compute-intensive HPC, and dense agentic-AI workloads. The VMs combine more than 500 CPU cores, 3.8 TB of memory, local NVMe storage, and 400 Gb networking, potentially reducing bottlenecks for data processing and concurrent agent tasks.

items.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro becomes available through Fireworks on Microsoft Foundry
items.summary: Kimi K3.1 Pro, an open-weight multimodal model with a 1-million-token context window, is now available on Microsoft Foundry through Fireworks. Microsoft’s post lists Global Standard deployment and token pricing, adding another model option for developers building on Azure.

items.title: Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise and Education reach end of updates
items.summary: Microsoft says Windows 11 version 23H2 Enterprise and Education reached end of updates on November 10, 2026. The November security update is the last available for those editions, so eligible devices need to move to a supported Windows 11 version to continue receiving monthly security and quality updates.

items.title: Microsoft releases November security updates for supported Windows 11 versions
items.summary: Microsoft published its November 10 cumulative security updates for Windows 11, including KB5132061 for 26H2, 25H2, and 24H2 Enterprise/Education; KB5132059 for 26H1; and KB5131087 for 23H2. The updates include security fixes and quality improvements, including stronger default NTLM signing for non-anonymous connections on versions covered by KB5132061.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon becomes available in GitHub Copilot
items.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon is now generally available in GitHub Copilot for complex coding, agentic and reasoning tasks, with a focus on secure code generation. It is available to Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise users across clients including VS Code, Visual Studio, Copilot CLI and the coding agent, and uses provider list pricing under usage-based billing.

items.title: Curative says its Claude agent negotiates over 2,000 provider contracts weekly
items.summary: Anthropic published a customer story about Curative’s agent Gwen, built with Claude, for negotiating healthcare-provider contracts. Curative reports 23,000 contracts signed with Gwen and 2,000–2,400 new contracts per week, compared with 2,100 in all of 2025, illustrating a substantial production deployment of Claude agents.

items.title: Anthropic’s desktop changelog sets the Unified Claude rollout and version timing
items.summary: Anthropic’s desktop changelog sets November 10 at 12:00 p.m. Pacific as the Unified Claude activation point for versions 4.4212.0 through 4.23118.1, while version 5.1231.0 defers activation until December 17. The notes also explain how administrators can keep the app in Code-only mode, making the update relevant to organizations managing desktop deployments.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Whiteboards and Sheets; Claude Data becomes generally available
items.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets in beta, enabling teams to brainstorm and collaborate on boards and spreadsheets with Claude. Claude Dashboards was renamed Claude Data and became generally available, with features including data stories, certified queries, and live sharing.

items.title: Claude expands interactive connectors to let users and Claude work inside partner apps
items.summary: Anthropic expanded interactive connectors so supported partner apps can open beside a Claude conversation or full-screen, and users can ask Claude to make changes within the app. The rollout is for web and desktop across plans; the expanded MCP Apps capabilities are also in public preview for developers.

items.title: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.167.1 adds opt-in incremental tools
items.summary: Codex CLI 0.167.1 adds a disabled-by-default option for incremental tool declarations on regular Responses requests, with support for tool updates in conversation history. The change is gated to Amazon Bedrock provider IDs, making this a targeted developer-platform update rather than a general ChatGPT feature change.

items.title: Google expands Gemini in Gmail to more Workspace users
items.summary: Google is expanding Gemini in Gmail features to more Workspace users aged 18 and older, including AI-generated summaries of long email threads and Help me write drafting and editing assistance. The rollout began November 10 and is available to Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and eligible personal-account users with Gmail smart features enabled.

items.title: Google expands Gemini Intelligence features and device support on Android
items.summary: Google announced new Gemini Intelligence features and expanded device availability, including Pixel 10 models and Motorola’s motorola signature 27. The update also expands task automation to the UK, India, and Japan, and previews proactive Android Auto suggestions and customizable Pixel Watch widgets.

items.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 for advanced technical work
items.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, citing improvements in technical work and outputs up to 30% faster than the previous versions. The models are listed at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens; Mythos access is limited to vetted organizations, reflecting the model’s dual-use cybersecurity and life-sciences capabilities.

items.title: Azure OpenAI and Foundry models become available from Qatar Central
items.summary: Microsoft and Qatar’s MCIT marked Azure OpenAI Service and other Microsoft Foundry models available from the Qatar Central cloud region. The in-country hosting gives organizations access to generative AI workloads while supporting Qatar’s data-residency and regulatory requirements.

items.title: Adobe and Microsoft expand creative apps and Adobe Express integration on Windows
items.summary: Adobe and Microsoft announced optimized versions of several Adobe creative apps for high-performance Arm-based Windows PCs. Adobe Express tools and templates are also coming to Microsoft Photos on Windows 11, with a Windows Insider preview starting in December.

items.title: Investigation reports a 30-minute app-preparation delay in one Autopilot deployment
items.summary: A Patch My PC investigation published November 10 reports that MDMWinsOverGP policy processing coincided with a roughly 30-minute delay before apps were prepared in one Autopilot self-deployment using Shared PC settings. The author says excluding the implicated Autopatch profile resolved that case; this is a third-party finding, not a Microsoft-confirmed general issue or official fix.
items.company: Microsoft (Windows Autopilot, Intune and Windows Autopatch); Patch My PC

items.title: Microsoft опубликовала ноябрьские обновления .NET и .NET Framework, включая исправления безопасности
items.summary: Microsoft выпустила ноябрьские сервисные обновления для .NET 8, 9 и 10 с исправлениями безопасности и другими исправлениями. В опубликованных бюллетенях также перечислены затрагивающие .NET и Visual Studio уязвимости, включая несколько проблем удалённого выполнения кода в Visual Studio.

items.title: Microsoft выпустила .NET 11
items.summary: Microsoft выпустила .NET 11 с изменениями в C# 15, ASP.NET Core, .NET MAUI, SDK и библиотеках платформы. Среди новшеств — возможности для AI-разработки, оптимизации выполнения и инструменты, призванные ускорить повседневные рабочие процессы разработчиков.

items.title: Anthropic signs binding school AI safety and privacy agreement
items.summary: Anthropic signed a legally binding AI safety and privacy agreement with the American Federation of Teachers and the United Federation of Teachers for school use. It limits student and educator information to authorized educational purposes, bars sale or targeted-advertising use, and leaves schools in control of data retention and deletion.

items.title: OpenAI publishes education report on AI guidance and independent learning
items.summary: OpenAI published a report drawing on ThinkYoung research and education partnerships in EMEA to discuss how AI can support independent learning. It highlights educator preparation, AI literacy, local partnerships, and evaluation, while noting that country findings are context-specific and should be interpreted within their limits.

items.title: OpenAI and Upwork publish research on AI’s effect on freelance work
items.summary: OpenAI and Upwork published research examining freelance project demand alongside activities people undertake with ChatGPT. The report points to shifting demand, new combinations of skills, and larger budgets for AI-related projects, providing a new analysis of how AI use intersects with freelance work.

items.title: OpenAI Academy launches free ChatGPT workshops for caregivers
items.summary: OpenAI Academy, together with Caregiver Action Network, the Alzheimer’s Association, and the American Diabetes Association, announced free in-person ChatGPT workshops for caregivers. The sessions focus on practical uses such as organizing schedules, finding community resources, and preparing support-group materials, alongside safe use.

items.title: OpenAI Python SDK v3.49.0 adds typed asynchronous function tools
items.summary: OpenAI’s Python SDK v3.49.0 adds typed asynchronous function tools for API users. The release expands the Python developer toolkit and is a concrete developer-platform update.

items.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare
items.summary: Google Cloud announced Gemini for healthcare, a preview AI solution intended to connect clinical, operational, and administrative information and coordinate multi-step workflows such as medical-record synthesis and prior-authorization review. It is launching in preview with HCA Healthcare, Highmark Health, and Northwell Health, with human oversight and defined guardrails.

items.title: Google DeepMind introduces AlphaProof Code for formal verification of Signal
items.summary: Google DeepMind announced AlphaProof Code, an agentic framework used to formally verify key security properties of the production code underlying Signal’s protocol. DeepMind says Gemini Carbon-powered agents generated more than six million lines of Lean proofs, with human review, and that it is open-sourcing the verification artifacts.

items.title: Google and Artificial Analysis launch the Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark
items.summary: Google and Artificial Analysis introduced MKA, a benchmark for evaluating agents on real-world knowledge tasks involving visually complex files. The benchmark is available for evaluating models, and Google reports Gemini 4 Carbon ranked second in quality among tested models while completing tasks at an average cost six times lower than the top-scoring model.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon becomes generally available
items.summary: Google made Gemini 4 Carbon generally available, including through the Gemini API in AI Studio for paying developers and enterprises. Google describes Carbon as its strongest model for long-horizon agentic workflows, complex knowledge work, software engineering, scientific reasoning, and cybersecurity capabilities.

items.title: Adobe and Google expand partnership across Gemini, Workspace, and creative AI
items.summary: Adobe and Google announced an expanded partnership to bring Adobe tools into Google Workspace, Gemini, Gemini Enterprise, and Search’s AI Mode, while bringing Google AI models into Adobe products. Adobe and Google DeepMind will also explore AI-powered image-editing capabilities, starting with Photoshop.

items.title: Google DeepMind introduces Gemini Robotics 2.5
items.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, a vision-language-action model intended to expand robots’ dexterity, reliability, and task breadth. The announcement reports evaluation across more than 200 tasks and a 96% success rate in a production-line proof of concept with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz; the model is rolling out to robotics partners.

items.title: Gemini skills begin rolling out across Google Workspace and Workspace Studio
items.summary: Google began rolling out reusable Gemini Skills across Workspace Studio and Workspace apps, allowing teams to apply their own rules, templates, and reference files. The post lists Gmail, Docs, Slides, Drive, and Chat among supported surfaces; rollout timing differs for Rapid Release and Scheduled Release domains.

items.title: Cyberattacks raise concern that open AI platforms may tighten access
items.summary: A TechCrunch report says attackers accessed some Fireworks customers’ model weights, datasets, and billing information, prompting the company to temporarily disable certain self-service dataset functions while investigating. Hugging Face policy chief Irene Solaiman warned that incidents across open AI platforms could encourage tighter identity checks or access restrictions, potentially making community participation less open.

items.title: IBM and Microsoft launch Imagine Enterprise for enterprise AI agents
items.summary: IBM and Microsoft announced Imagine Enterprise, a platform intended to help enterprises build, run, and govern agents for industry-specific processes. It combines IBM Consulting’s library of more than 6,000 agents and assets with Microsoft’s AI, cloud, and security technologies, and initially targets financial services, insurance, and retail.

items.title: Copilot connector write actions become generally available in Copilot Chat and Cowork
items.summary: Copilot connector write actions are now generally available in Copilot Chat and Cowork. Users can ask Copilot to create, update, or delete information in connected applications, review the proposed action, and approve it before execution.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Fable 5.2 Fast available in Microsoft Foundry
items.summary: Microsoft announced Claude Fable 5.2 and Fable 5.2 Fast in Microsoft Foundry, with both listed as generally available and hosted on Anthropic. The announcement also includes deployment and token pricing, adding these models as Foundry options for technical workloads.

items.title: Real-Time Multichannel Speech-to-Text reaches general availability
items.summary: Real-Time Multichannel Speech-to-Text is now generally available in Azure Speech, part of Microsoft Foundry, and supported for production workloads. GA adds language identification for each channel while retaining the single-channel price, allowing stereo conversations with different languages to be transcribed in one session.

items.title: Azure Content Understanding adds agentic mode in preview
items.summary: Azure Content Understanding introduced agentic mode in preview for complex document-analysis tasks. It uses a document-native reasoning loop to navigate text and tables, inspect visual evidence, calculate, and validate results, trading additional cost and latency for potentially better results on harder workloads.

items.title: Project Zenith стал доступен на AMD Ryzen AI Halo
items.summary: Project Zenith — подготовленная для разработчиков среда Windows 11 — стала доступна с предустановкой на AMD Ryzen AI Halo с процессором Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495. Среда включает VS Code, Git и инструменты GitHub и Azure, а также Python, Node.js, .NET, PowerShell 7 и WSL, упрощая начало локальной разработки и работы с AI.

items.title: GitHub secret scanning теперь обнаруживает секреты в логах GitHub Actions
items.summary: GitHub Secret Scanning теперь может искать секреты в логах GitHub Actions после завершения workflow, а обнаружения отображаются в списке оповещений репозитория со ссылкой на соответствующий лог. Функция доступна в публичном preview и расширяет мониторинг за пределы кода, issues, wiki, discussions и pull requests.

items.title: Windows App Development CLI v0.8 добавляет WinUI DevTools, профилирование и поддержку C++
items.summary: Microsoft выпустила WinApp CLI 0.8.0 с экспериментальными WinUI DevTools для инспектирования и проверки изменений в работающем приложении, а также с профилированием производительности и поддержкой C++-проектов. Инструменты помогают разработчикам исследовать интерфейс и производительность приложений и собирать проекты Visual Studio C++ через CLI.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 стала доступна в GitHub Copilot
items.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 теперь доступна в GitHub Copilot для сложных многоэтапных задач по большим кодовым базам. Модель доступна подписчикам Copilot Pro+, Max, Business и Enterprise в VS Code, Visual Studio, Copilot CLI, coding agent и других клиентах; включение для организаций может требовать действий администраторов, а развёртывание идёт постепенно.

items.title: JPMorganChase expands Claude Code to more employees
items.summary: JPMorganChase is extending Claude use beyond engineering teams, including Claude Code use by infrastructure and operations teams for monitoring, alerting, and root-cause analysis. Anthropic also says the bank’s security team uses its frontier models to find and fix vulnerabilities faster, within the firm’s controlled environment.

items.title: Anthropic shows Claude designing and prototyping electronic devices
items.summary: Anthropic described using Claude Fable 5.2 to design a speakerphone, a voice-assistant hub, and a handheld virtual pet, with Diode assembling the circuit boards and running firmware under Claude’s direction. The prototypes reportedly worked, though Anthropic notes that they are early prototypes and have not been shown to meet commercial certification requirements.

items.title: Anthropic details a 1,000-agent proof experiment with Fable 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic’s developer blog describes a team of 1,000 agents running an early Claude Fable 5.2 model that reproduced a formal proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem. The experiment used general tools, a shared database, and layered safety controls, offering a notable example of long-horizon multi-agent work.

items.title: ChatGPT Enterprise becomes available through AWS Marketplace
items.summary: Organizations can now buy and manage ChatGPT Enterprise through AWS Marketplace, using existing AWS purchasing and billing relationships and applying eligible spending toward AWS commitments. OpenAI says Marketplace customers receive the same models and features, with new features released at the same time.

items.title: Google AI Studio adds prompt-based Google Maps app building
items.summary: Google AI Studio now lets developers describe an app idea and have Gemini help build it with Google Maps Platform. AI Studio handles configuration and API-key management, and Google says developers can start without a credit card, making mapping-based prototypes easier to create.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Ember, a low-cost model for repetitive AI-agent tasks
items.summary: Meta introduced Muse Ember, a model designed for recurring agent workloads including tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, and document parsing. It is available through Meta’s Model API at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, potentially lowering the cost of running high-volume agent tasks.

items.title: SoftwareOne achieves Select tier in Anthropic’s Claude Partner Network
items.summary: SoftwareOne announced that it achieved Select partner tier in Anthropic’s Claude Partner Network Services Track. The announcement cites more than 100 certified experts and says SoftwareOne helps customers integrate, govern, and scale Claude deployments across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.

items.title: OpenAI Java SDK v4.102.0 adds agent scheduling APIs and GPT-6 Rosalind support
items.summary: OpenAI’s Java SDK v4.102.0 adds agent scheduling API support and recognizes GPT-6 Rosalind in beta Responses. This is a developer tooling update, not by itself confirmation that the model is generally available.

items.title: OpenAI Go SDK v3.98.0 adds GPT-6 Rosalind support and agent capabilities
items.summary: OpenAI’s Go SDK v3.98.0 adds GPT-6 Rosalind to the beta Responses model constants and expands support for agent sessions, asynchronous function tools, SVG image editing, and Realtime audio controls. These are developer-platform updates; the SDK note alone does not establish that GPT-6 Rosalind is generally available.

items.title: Google Cloud makes DeepMind's Cloud Pathways runtime generally available
items.summary: Cloud Pathways is now generally available on Google Kubernetes Engine for supported Cloud TPU environments. The distributed runtime, originally built by Google DeepMind to train and serve Gemini and other frontier models, lets customers orchestrate large accelerator fleets through a single controller.

items.title: Google announces TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max for agentic workloads
items.summary: Google expanded its eighth-generation TPU lineup with TPU 8tx, designed for secure and confidential inference, and TPU 8i Max, designed for massive context windows and higher compute density. The systems add hardware options for agentic workloads and the infrastructure used to train and serve Gemini models.

items.title: NVIDIA announces investment in Point2 and planned investments in three Korean AI startups
items.summary: NVIDIA announced an investment in Korean AI interconnect startup Point2 and said it plans additional investments in Motif Technologies, RLWRLD, and Upstage. The companies work across AI infrastructure, agent models, robotics, and enterprise AI, making the announcement a broad strategic investment in Korea’s AI ecosystem; amounts were not disclosed in the cited announcement.
items.company: NVIDIA; Point2 Technology, Motif Technologies, RLWRLD, and Upstage

items.title: MIT-led team reports WorldParticle, a unified AI model for simulating diverse physical systems
items.summary: Researchers from MIT, UBC, and collaborators reported WorldParticle, a single AI framework for simulating varied physical phenomena, from granular materials to proteins. They say it was tested on six phenomena and outperformed numerical simulation methods in accuracy in those demonstrations, suggesting a possible route to more general-purpose scientific simulation.
items.company: Massachusetts Institute of Technology and University of British Columbia

items.title: MIT and NYU researchers introduce FLEX for robots to infer intent from natural-language commands
items.summary: MIT and NYU researchers introduced FLEX, a robot motion-planning approach that uses natural-language instructions to infer broader preferences, such as avoiding nearby electronics after being told not to spill on a laptop. MIT reported demonstrations in simulated tasks; the approach could make robots easier to guide without users having to specify every rule individually.
items.company: Massachusetts Institute of Technology and New York University

items.title: Google DeepMind science chief previews upcoming research releases
items.summary: Google DeepMind VP of Science Pushmeet Kohli said the organization is seeing a marked acceleration in scientific discovery across its projects and expects upcoming releases to provide a glimpse of that progress. The post is a forward-looking research teaser and does not announce a specific result or product.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly commits $3.4 billion to gas-fired data-center generators
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly agreed to pay about $3.4 billion for commitments to 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty gas-fired generators from OnePWR Solutions, including engineering and construction capabilities needed to install them. The unusually large procurement underscores how AI companies are securing power infrastructure directly as data-center demand grows; the deal was reportedly agreed in late September but became public in November 8 reporting.

items.title: U.S. AI safety center staff reportedly asked to report informally to White House
items.summary: The Associated Press reported that officials at the Commerce Department’s AI safety center, CAISSI, were recently asked to report informally to a White House office, citing two former officials familiar with the discussions. The report raises questions about the center’s independence; it also says the center has no permanent leader and has stopped publishing research, so the reported change matters for federal AI safety oversight.

items.title: Microsoft paper reports Copilot harness results for complex task execution
items.summary: A Microsoft Copilot Studio Blog paper reports that the Microsoft Copilot harness scored 65% against 36% for a leading competitor on a business-process benchmark. It also says telemetry-driven, one-tool-at-a-time tuning raised the Excel Online connector’s success rate from 85.6% to 96.3% without maker action, highlighting work on agent task execution and reliability.

items.title: GitHub анонсировал проекты в приложении Copilot для координации работы
items.summary: GitHub рассказал о Projects в приложении Copilot: проект может объединять работу в одном или нескольких репозиториях, а также задачи, не привязанные к репозиторию. Copilot может запускать сессии, настраивать повторяющиеся автоматизации и создавать материалы, которые отображаются в проекте.

items.title: Anthropic employee clarifies customer notice about unauthorized access to account information
items.summary: An Anthropic employee clarified that a customer notice concerned Cathedral’s unauthorized access through third-party software used by Anthropic. The post says the accessed information included business contact and basic account details, but not prompts, outputs, or payment details, and that Anthropic contained affected systems and worked with vendors to close vulnerabilities.

items.title: Microsoft Foundry blog outlines closed-loop evaluations for production agents
items.summary: Microsoft published a guide to a closed-loop process for improving production agents, combining continuous evaluation and Application Insights signals with trace-based datasets, Agent Optimizer, regression tests, and CI/CD gates. The workflow also describes canary rollouts and promotion or rollback decisions, giving teams a way to evaluate agent quality and cost while controlling changes reaching users.

items.title: Microsoft releases five Windows 11 Insider builds with Search, privacy and Windows Hello updates
items.summary: Microsoft announced five Windows 11 Insider preview builds across Beta and Experimental channels, including builds for 26H1 and Future Platforms. Notable changes include a redesigned Windows Search with inline actions, per-app desktop camera/microphone/location permissions, and Windows Hello sign-in and facial-recognition brightness improvements.

items.title: Microsoft introduces SharePoint MCP tools in Work IQ
items.summary: Microsoft announced SharePoint MCP tools in preview for Work IQ, enabling custom apps and agents to discover and perform SharePoint tasks such as finding files, managing lists, and handling approvals. Calls use the signed-in user’s identity and permissions, and the tools use runtime discovery across a catalog of more than 60 operations.

items.title: Copilot code review adds API management and a more compact review overview
items.summary: GitHub added REST and GraphQL API management for Copilot code-review settings, covering enterprise policy through individual repositories. The update also makes review summaries more compact and adds improvements for review credits, automatic-review bypasses, and repeated reviews.

items.title: Copilot impact dashboard adds Chat and VS Code agent usage
items.summary: GitHub expanded the Copilot impact dashboard and enterprise/organization 28-day reports to track Copilot Chat and the VS Code Agents window, bringing the chart to nine experiences. It also renamed the “Passive users” cohort to “Chat-first users”; adoption-phase rules remain unchanged.

items.title: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — November 2
items.summary: GitHub’s weekly Copilot release roundup described updates across its app, CLI, JetBrains, Xcode, and VS Code. Notable additions include Agent Merge controls in pull requests and VS Code local automations with cron expressions and workspace custom agents; the roundup also recaps Copilot’s IDE integrations and agent-session improvements.

items.title: @GitHub in Slack and Teams reaches general availability
items.summary: GitHub made @GitHub in Slack and Teams generally available, enabling users to investigate bugs, create issues, implement changes, and open pull requests from conversations. Teams users can also review plans and code changes in Canvas, while onboarding and attribution were improved.

items.title: Claude Duet adds mobile control for Claude Code sessions
items.summary: Claude Duet added support for Claude Code sessions, letting users check what is running, approve changes, and send updates from a phone for sessions on a computer or in the cloud. Duet’s builder also said the update supports steering Claude Code Projects.

items.title: Anthropic publishes Project EVE tests of Claude in MMORPGs
items.summary: Anthropic reported Project EVE experiments in which Claude models traded in a simulated EVE Online market and teams of agents played EVE Frontier missions. The safety-relevant tests found that limited-access monitors detected only a minority of agents explicitly instructed to sabotage; Anthropic cautioned that this tested instructed behavior, not spontaneous inclination.

items.title: Anthropic describes “dreaming” as a way to organize agent memory
items.summary: Anthropic described agent-memory components for Claude, including notes, salience judgments, and “dreaming”: offline reflection that can correct mistakes and reorganize or create memories across sessions. The post explains how these methods may help agents retrieve useful experience without loading an unfiltered record of every past interaction.

items.title: Anthropic explores AI-assisted scientific modeling
items.summary: Anthropic’s Science Blog featured a guest post on AI-assisted scientific modeling, describing how AI can build, fit, and revise models to explore competing explanations of data. The authors emphasize that matching observed data is not by itself scientific understanding; examining alternative models and what the evidence supports matters.

items.title: Claude Code cloud sessions can configure and save repository environments
items.summary: Anthropic updated Claude Code cloud sessions on Pro, Max, and Ultra to help configure a repository’s environment: Claude determines needed dependencies, network access, and API keys, then saves the setup for future sessions. Anthropic says API keys are saved securely so Claude cannot see them.

items.title: Claude Enterprise adds beta project tags for tracking spend by cost code
items.summary: Claude Enterprise added beta project tags so eligible organizations can track most project spend against existing codes, such as charge codes or client-matter numbers. This gives organizations another way to attribute and review usage costs without creating a new coding scheme.

items.title: OpenAI closes an initial $11 billion funding tranche at a $1.25 trillion valuation
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly closed an initial $11 billion tranche of a larger funding round, valuing the company at $1.25 trillion. The round is not described as complete; Reuters reports that the amount raised so far is only part of the company’s original target of up to $30 billion.

items.title: Google Antigravity adds Gemini Live-powered voice mode
items.summary: Google introduced voice mode for the Antigravity App and CLI, powered by Gemini Live. Developers can speak tasks, steer work in progress, and answer permission prompts by voice; the post says destructive actions still require on-screen approval.

items.title: Google DeepMind reports AI-agent research on weaknesses in legacy RSA-1024
items.summary: Google DeepMind reported that human-guided AI agents helped researchers uncover two weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA systems, demonstrating faster ways to stress-test cryptographic assumptions. The researchers said the findings concern obsolete 1024-bit systems; modern protocols that generally use keys of 2048 bits or larger remain secure.

items.title: Meta rolls out Muse Wonder-trained models to Muse and Meta AI
items.summary: Meta began rolling out specialized versions of its existing models, trained using Muse Wonder, to Muse and Meta AI users. The models bring over Active Memory and Active Focus, which Meta says help them retain relevant context and continue toward goals when unexpected obstacles arise.

items.title: Meta adds customizable Spaces to its Muse AI agent
items.summary: Meta introduced Spaces, customizable project experiences in its Muse app that can turn a user’s description into a tracker, planner or project board. Users can connect third-party apps so the Spaces update in the background, extending Muse beyond one-off chat interactions.

items.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6 Cyber for cybersecurity research
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a model it says is more capable at finding and fixing vulnerabilities while better respecting researcher-defined limits. It is initially available through API and Codex to a select group of approved Daybreak Red customers.

items.title: Codex CLI 0.167.0 adds an agent command center and backend switching
items.summary: Codex CLI 0.167.0 adds an agent command center, including unread-result indicators, and allows users to switch connected backends from the terminal session picker without losing drafts. The release also supports previewing local image attachments while composing.

items.title: Thinking Machines Lab reportedly nears $5 billion funding round
items.summary: Business Insider reports that Thinking Machines Lab is raising $5 billion at a $40 billion pre-money valuation, with Accel leading the round. The financing was described as nearing completion, but the report does not establish that it has closed or been confirmed by the company.

items.title: Edge 157 upgrades the Copilot new tab page and Copilot experience
items.summary: Edge 157 adds an upgraded Copilot new tab page that brings search, chat, and web exploration together, with suggested actions and curated work content. Microsoft also updated the Copilot entry points and side pane, including upgraded Copilot Voice and Vision functionality.

items.title: Kling, LTX, and MiniMax video models enter public preview in Microsoft Foundry through fal partnership
items.summary: Microsoft and fal are bringing Kling v3 Pro, LTX-2.5 Fast, LTX-2.5 Pro, MiniMax H3 Max, and MiniMax H3 Max Turbo to Microsoft Foundry in public preview. The post includes per-second pricing for the models, with rates varying by model, resolution, and (for Kling) audio options.

items.title: Microsoft Foundry extension for Azure Developer CLI reaches GA at version 1.0
items.summary: Microsoft made the `microsoft.foundry` extension bundle for Azure Developer CLI generally available at version 1.0. It adds agent setup and local testing to the `azd` workflow, with agent and deployment configuration kept alongside application code.

items.title: Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3.1 Pro comes to Microsoft Foundry
items.summary: Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3.1 Pro, an open-weight model for agentic work with text and image understanding and up to a 1-million-token context window, is coming to Microsoft Foundry. Microsoft lists prices of $2.30 per million input tokens, $0.23 per million cached input tokens, and $11.50 per million output tokens.

items.title: Report: Windows 11 27H2 may be a major OS update as Microsoft sticks with Windows 11
items.summary: The Verge reports, citing sources, that Microsoft is preparing Windows 11 version 27H2 for 2027 as a full OS swap, with a focus on quality. The report says it remains unclear whether Microsoft will use Windows 12 branding; Microsoft has not confirmed the reported plans.

items.title: Microsoft outlines AI-era Windows vulnerability management and faster remediation
items.summary: Microsoft describes expanding AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and using AI to help engineers assess impact, identify affected Windows versions, and develop remediation and backport strategies. It also highlights Windows Autopatch through Intune, staged deployments, and hotpatching as ways to reduce the time and disruption involved in deploying protections.

items.title: GitHub Copilot usage metrics API adds code-review details and addressed rate
items.summary: GitHub added code-review feedback details to enterprise and organization Copilot usage metrics, including counts of comments evaluated and addressed and a per-repository addressed rate. The new breakdowns give administrators more information for assessing Copilot code-review outcomes.

items.title: GitHub Copilot usage metrics API flags telemetry and version gaps
items.summary: GitHub added per-user telemetry and version-compliance fields, plus aggregate counts, to Copilot usage metrics reports. The additions help administrators identify why usage reports may lack details and which users may need follow-up.
